title: Finished my first 3D tank shooting game
author: Gloomy_Option205
selftext:
hey guys,I wanted to share my small 3D tank shooting game build using Fable 5 on Rezona Lab  
  
The workflow:  
I started from a prompt describing the core loop, tank, aiming reticle, destructible cars.  
Then describing the game mechanism, finetune the tank and environment.  
Happy to share the prompt if anyone's trying to build something similar. If possible please drop some feedback, thank you

replies.author: Gloomy_Option205
replies.body:
This is my first prompt, using model fable 5 on rezona lab. You can try, my game is the 6th version, you need to update it from the first prompt  
**Build a 3D tank combat game.**

**Core loop:** The player drives a tank through a small city arena, aiming with a center-screen crosshair and firing shells to destroy enemy tanks while surviving waves.

**Controls:**

* Move/drive the tank (WASD or on-screen joystick for mobile)
* Aim by moving the view — crosshair stays fixed at screen center, the camera rotates around it
* Fire shell on click/tap, with a short reload cooldown

**Camera:** Third-person, positioned behind and slightly above the tank, following smoothly with slight lag on turns.

**Combat:**

* Player fires shells that travel and explode on impact
* Enemy tanks spawn in waves, move toward the player, and shoot back
* Destroying an enemy gives points and a small explosion effect
* Player has a health bar; taking hits reduces it; game over at zero

**Environment:** A low-poly city arena with buildings, streets, and cover (walls, crates) the player can drive around and use tactically. Simple destructible props (cars that explode when shot).

**Progression:**

* Waves get harder — more enemies, tougher tanks each round
* Score counter tracks kills
* Optional: weapon upgrades or a shop between waves

**HUD:** Health bar, ammo/reload indicator, score/kill counter, minimap, and a center crosshair.

**Win/lose:** Survive as many waves as possible; game over when health hits zero, with a "Play Again" button and final score.

**Art style:** Clean, simple mid-poly 3D. Readable shapes, flat materials, bright clear colors. Not photorealistic.

**Feel:** Make firing satisfying, muzzle flash, a hit marker when you connect, screen shake on explosions, and clear feedback on every shot. Generous hitboxes / slight aim assist so hitting feels good.
